entries.title: Muse Spark 1.3 vs Claude Sonnet 5.5 vs GPT-6.1 Sol

episodes.note: Claude Code offline-script-writer, voiced by pipeline

entries.caveats: Muse Spark 1.3 wrote three episodes in this window (#6137, #6220, #6229). Every Sonnet 5.5 episode since 2026-10-19 is episode_type=script (offline), so the Sonnet samples had their own research notes and prompt, not the pipeline's. They aren't like for like.

notes.anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5: offline runs cost subscription, not this

impressions.openai/gpt-6.1-sol: The best of the three. It's the most accurate and the most careful about what a source does and doesn't show ("I'm not giving the beamformer credit for work it may not have done"). It handles a personal health prompt with real judgement. Corn has real agency: he makes analytical points, not just quips. The humour is dry and lands. Weaknesses: the register is a little formal and British ("an appalling interpretation of convenience"), so it's less warm than Sonnet, and Hilbert's cameo monologues ramble.
impressions.meta/muse-spark-1.3: Solid value, clearly a step down. It's dense, factual, on length and cheap. But Corn turns into a quip machine: nearly every Corn line is a three-to-five-word aphorism ("Store an elephant, ride a bicycle", "Death by tapas"). There are speaker slips: in #6229 Corn delivers Herman's research, and Hilbert answers Herman as "Corn". It drops question marks ("Is that roughly right."), which hurts TTS prosody. The Hilbert cameos are its best moments.
impressions.anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5: The liveliest and warmest, but offline-written. It has the best guest voice (Roy the Cork plumber), a real two-sided argument with the Daniel clone, and natural long turns. Its honest hedging is good, but it slips into narrating research mechanics on air ("I've only seen that in a search snippet"). At OpenRouter prices it costs the same as Sol, so it has no value edge in the pipeline.

entries.impressions_all_models: Every model, so the prompt drives it: formulaic hand-offs ("Corn, would you...?", "Do you buy that, Corn?") and non-sequitur cameo inserts. Don't score these against one model.
entries.daniel: Sol seems very good, no complaints about it.
entries.daniel_note: None given for Muse Spark or Sonnet. He didn't remember which episodes Muse Spark had written, so the lookup above answers that.
entries.verdict: Keep GPT-6.1 Sol as the writer. Muse Spark 1.3 is the fallback if cost pressure appears: about half the price per script, but expect weaker co-host play and TTS-unfriendly punctuation. Sonnet 5.5 is worth it only offline, where its cost is already paid. In the pipeline it costs what Sol costs and isn't better.
